flashgaze.tagline: An AI-assisted local image-scoring CLI — objective CV metrics as the foundation, vision LLMs compensating on demand, built for stable invocation by AI agents

overview.title: Overview
overview.b0: Picking the best few dozen shots out of hundreds is slow and subjective. FlashGaze automates it: a CV engine objectively measures sharpness and exposure on your own machine, an optional vision-LLM layer decides whether blur or darkness is an artistic choice (background bokeh, backlit silhouettes, low-key mood) or a technical mistake, and the result is a sorted, reasoned, structured report you can plug straight into any workflow.
overview.b1: It is CLI-first: clean JSON on stdout, logs on stderr, standard exit codes — naturally suited to stable subprocess invocation by AI agents. A Gradio-based browser GUI and a built-in MCP Server are also included, so photographers, developers, and AI assistants all find a way of working that suits them.

b2.title: Zero-cost mode
b2.text: Add --no-vlm to run fully offline: no API key, no data sent anywhere, and the same image scored 10 times in a row returns identical scores (10/10 reproducibility verified).

how.title: How it works

b0.note: Side path: VLMClient (optional) feeds into HybridScorer, supporting four provider types: Qwen-VL / GPT-4o / Claude 3 / Ollama.

rows: Laplacian variance, linear mapping, capped at 500
Histogram midtone ratio (penalizes extreme dark / bright pixels)
Rule of thirds + Otsu foreground centroid (experimental)
Face count + sharpness bonus for face regions (requires face_recognition)
PHash perceptual hashing, keeps only the highest score per similar group (requires imagededup)

how.b2: Default weights are 50% sharpness + 50% exposure. When optional dimensions are enabled without an explicit --weights, a sensible set of default weights is injected automatically (e.g. all enabled → sharpness 0.35 / exposure 0.25 / composition 0.20 / noise 0.10 / color 0.10); --weights also allows full customization.

b3.title: VLM adjustment mechanism
b3.text: The VLM receives both the image and the CV metrics, judges whether blur or darkness is creative intent or a shooting mistake, and returns a signed adjustment capped at ±10 points, added to the CV weighted score and clamped to 0–100. Whenever the adjustment is non-zero, the output must include a reason of ≤20 characters (vlm_reason) and the provider identifier (vlm_provider) — every point is traceable.

b0.title: Hybrid scoring engine
b0.description: Objective CV scores (Laplacian variance + histogram exposure) form the base and dominate the result; VLM scene adjustments are capped at ±10 points — aesthetics get a voice, but never overturn the verdict.

b0.title: Explainable scores
b0.description: Every VLM adjustment comes with a Chinese reason of ≤20 characters and a provider identifier, written into the JSON / CSV output — every single point can be traced.

b0.title: Scene-aware scoring
b0.description: --scene switches between differentiated prompts for the four scenes auto / portrait / landscape / still_life, so adjustments fit the subject matter.

b0.title: Multiple VLM providers
b0.description: Qwen-VL by default with zero added dependencies; GPT-4o, Claude 3, and Ollama connect through a unified LiteLLM layer — no vendor-specific adapter code.

b0.title: Agent-friendly
b0.description: Pure JSON on stdout, logs on stderr, standard exit codes — a subprocess can json.loads the output directly, and batch runs stay stable without surprising the caller.

b0.title: Zero-cost offline
b0.description: --no-vlm mode never touches the network and needs no API key — ideal for bulk first-pass filtering and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

b0.title: Graceful degradation
b0.description: Broken images return score=0 with an error field; VLM failures fall back to pure CV automatically — no single point of failure interrupts a batch run.

b0.title: Built-in MCP Server
b0.description: Install the [mcp] extra, add one config snippet to your AI tool, and it can directly invoke scoring, selection, export, and workspace cleanup.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.b1: The JSON report contains a summary (total count, selected count, average score, elapsed time) plus per-image metrics; the selected field marks the picks and can directly drive downstream export and automation.

vlm.title: VLM providers
vlm.b0: Four provider types connect through a unified calling layer with no vendor-specific adapter code: qwen (default) uses a native requests path with zero added dependencies; the other three go through the unified LiteLLM layer. All providers take their key from the FLASHGAZE_API_KEY environment variable (Ollama needs no real key — any non-empty value works).

rows: Leave empty to use the LiteLLM default endpoint

b3.title: Graceful degradation
b3.text: If LiteLLM is not installed and a non-qwen provider is selected, VLM calls return a litellm_not_installed error and automatically fall back to pure CV mode while the batch completes as usual; invalid provider / scene values fall back to defaults with a warning logged.

scene.title: Scene-aware scoring
scene.b0: --scene switches the VLM prompt so adjustments focus on the artistic techniques of different subjects; auto (default) lets the VLM determine the scene itself, semantically identical to the original single prompt.

mcp.title: MCP Server
mcp.b0: After installing the [mcp] extra, add the configuration below to your AI tool's MCP settings and the assistant can drive every FlashGaze capability directly:

mcp.b3: Once configured, just tell the assistant: "Evaluate the image quality in this directory", "Pick the best 30 photos", or "Clean up the low-quality images in the workspace".

b4.title: Workspace cleanup safety
b4.text: Deletion in cleanup_workspace_images is strictly confined to the workspace directory: real paths are resolved and the boundary is double-checked with relative_to, dry_run=True is the default so it only reports the pending deletion list without deleting, and every file's path is re-validated before deletion.

gui.title: Web GUI
gui.b0: A Gradio-based browser interface maps every CLI option to a UI control, and scoring reuses the same HybridScorer assembly chain — for the same directory and options, GUI and CLI results are byte-identical. By default it is reachable only from the local machine (127.0.0.1:7860); LAN access requires explicitly passing --host 0.0.0.0.

b4.title: Offline mode
b4.text: Check "Disable VLM (pure offline CV scoring)" to complete the entire scoring flow without an API key, exactly matching flashgaze --no-vlm; the VLM settings section is then disabled automatically to prevent ineffective configuration.

config.title: Configuration & exit codes
config.b0: Configuration precedence: CLI flags > environment variables > config file (config.example.json) > defaults; the weights field can only be set in the config file.

rows: VLM API key (not needed in --no-vlm mode)
VLM retry count (timeouts / connection errors only)
API call failure (reserved — VLM failures already degrade to pure CV)
Image processing error (reserved — corrupt images already degrade to the error field)

config.b3: Exit codes 2 and 4 are reserved: VLM call failures degrade to pure CV (adjustment 0), and corrupt images degrade to that image's error field with score=0 — neither interrupts the batch.

quality.title: Testing & tech stack
quality.b0: The full pytest suite has 1076 cases (1076 passed / 29 skipped, coverage 90.49% ≥ the 80% gate), covering the CV engine, VLM client, hybrid scorer, exporter, CLI parser, end-to-end flows, reproducibility, the configuration layer, and cleanup safety — reproducible, explainable scores are not just a slogan.

rows: CV scoring (Laplacian variance, histograms, Otsu thresholding)

nikki-gallery.tagline: A Windows desktop photo-album manager built for Infinity Nikki players — scan, browse, edit, organize, and share in one place, with all data kept local

overview.title: Overview
overview.b0: MeowStarMap (formerly NikkiGallery) is a Windows desktop photo-album manager designed for Infinity Nikki players: it automatically scans game screenshots and recordings, and provides professional image browsing, editing, categorization, and search — covering the full album workflow in one place.
overview.b1: All data is stored locally and nothing is uploaded to any cloud — every outfit creation in your album belongs to you alone.

b2.title: Local-first
b2.text: Scan indexes, edit results, and category profiles are all stored in a local SQLite database on your machine — nothing is uploaded to the cloud.

b0.title: Smart scanning
b0.description: Automatically locates the game directory (Steam / Epic registry + full-disk signature scanning), with incremental scans and concurrent multi-drive processing; intelligently distinguishes three sources: game screenshots, launcher cache, and cloud album.

b0.title: Multi-view gallery
b0.description: Five browsing modes — grid, list, masonry, timeline, and event timeline — plus fullscreen viewing and slideshow playback, with Ctrl / Shift multi-select for batch operations.

b0.title: Professional image editing
b0.description: 14 basic adjustments + independent HSL eight-color grading + multi-channel RGB curves + split toning + filter presets, with full undo / redo and batch application.

b0.title: Video processing
b0.description: Thumbnail extraction, video trimming, 0.25x–4x speed control, format conversion, and Apple Live Photo export.

b0.title: Smart organization
b0.description: System categories + a three-level custom category tree (drag-to-sort / color labels), tag management, and five smart grouping dimensions (album type / scene / time of day / outfit / type).

b0.title: Resonance Log (new in 2.5.0)
b0.description: Browse and manually backfill gacha records, track wardrobe ownership and outfit collection progress, import/export local JSON, and view personal statistics; gacha and wardrobe data run fully offline.

b0.title: Device sync (new in 2.5.5)
b0.description: A built-in NikkiSync protocol v1 server pairs and authenticates over LAN HTTPS + WebSocket so mobile devices can sync directly with the local media library; the "Sync Gallery" section is off by default.

b0.title: Duplicate detection
b0.description: Dual detection with SHA256 exact comparison + perceptual hashing (pHash), and four-dimension smart scoring to recommend which copy to keep.

b0.title: Sharing & backup
b0.description: Clipboard sharing to WeChat / QQ / vivo + WiFi LAN transfer (PIN authentication); automatic scheduled backups plus manual backups, with 5-copy LRU rotation.

more.title: More capabilities
more.b0: Beyond the core album features, a set of companion capabilities makes long-term use easier:

b1.title: Character profiles

b1.title: Diagnostics
b1.description: Built-in diagnostics give troubleshooting something solid to rely on.
